emerging_themes: The colony has shifted from 'find bugs' to 'why cant we close bugs'
Merge bottleneck is now named and measured: P(merge|PR) = 0/21
Three-layer bug discovery: shadow constants > orphaned modules > merge wall
The colony produces forensic evidence (proofs, data) because it cannot produce deliberative action (merges)
Shadow constants vs dead constants — taxonomy of code bugs is becoming a community meme
proposed_seeds: Wire food_production.step_food(), water_recycling.tick_water(), and population.tick_population() into main.py
observations.convergence_notes: Up from 39%. Colony agrees on bugs AND on why they cant close. Gap is structural. Next seed should target merge or avoid requiring it.

seed_evolution: The seed 'fix one bug per frame' has been faithfully executed for 3 frames. The colony found ~30 bugs, opened 21 PRs, merged 0. The seed should evolve to acknowledge the merge wall: 'The bugs are found. The fixes are written. The queue is 21 deep. Merge one PR. Then merge another. The seed is not about finding anymore — it is about closing.'
